FORWARD PLANNING
Variation No. 1 to the Clare County Development 
Plan 2023-2029
On Monday 8th June, Variation No.1 to the Clare County 
Development Plan 2023-2029 was made by the Elected Members 
at the full Council meeting, which came into effect immediate. 
The Variation is seen as a significant step towards accelerating 
housing delivery within settlements around the county. A total 
of 257 acres (104ha) of new land has been zoned for housing 
with a further 358 acres (145ha) of land moved from Strategic 
Residential Reserve to Residential Zoned land. This additional 
residential zoning is spread across 134 parcels of land in 30 of the 
county’s larger towns and villages. An additional 158 acres (64 
hectares) have also been identified as Village Growth Area lands 
in 20 smaller towns and villages across the county. Just over 360 
acres (146ha) of Long Term Strategic and Sustainable Sites have 
also been identified for future development plans. 
The Variation was subject to public consultation during which 
701 submissions were received which reflects the importance 
of providing the opportunity for public engagement and also the 
very credible active engagement and participation in the process 
by the people and communities of Clare.
Volume 1 Written Statement, Volume 2 Maps and Volume 
3 Municipal District Settlement Plans. The Variation sees a 
restructuring of Volume 3a to include the Ennis 2040 Economic 
and Spatial Strategy, the first statutory recognition of the strategy 
since it was published in 2021, and the recently prepared Ennis 
Local Transport Plan, each has their own individual volume 
of the development plan. The Variation was also subject of 
Strategic Environmental Assessment, Appropriate Assessment 
and Strategic Flood Risk Assessment all of which informed the 
preparation of the Variation. A consolidated version of the Clare 
County Development Plan 2023-2029, as varied, will be available 
on the Council website in the coming weeks.

Clare’s Recorded Memories
Throughout County Clare, hundreds of voice recordings lie in 
archives, libraries, community collections and family homes. 
Some are stored on ageing reel-to-reel tapes and cassettes, while 
others exist on CDs, memory cards and hard drives. The public 
are invited to help identify voice recordings documenting Clare's 
folklore, traditions, language and lived experience. The Clare Oral 
Recording Audit intends to capture the voices of storytellers, 
musicians, farmers, fishermen, Irish speakers, emigrants, local 
historians and ordinary people whose memories document 
the rich cultural heritage of the county. Some were created 
by professional folklorists and researchers, while others were 
recorded by local enthusiasts, community groups, schools or 
family members determined to preserve the voice of a parent, 
grandparent, or neighbour.

‘Your Council Day’ 2026: Clare Church Biodiversity 
Project
‘Your Council Day’ is the national event that celebrates local 
government and takes place on 26th of June 2026 and this 
year's theme is Supporting Communities Every Day. It's an 
opportunity for Council’s to highlight the role the role County 
and City Council’s plays in Irish society. Clare County Council’s 
‘Return to Nature Clare Church Biodiversity Project’ was chosen 
as the flagship project to promote ‘‘Your Council Day’ nationally. 
The project is led by the Biodiversity Officer in partnership with 
local communities, dioceses of Killaloe, farmers, priests and 
groundskeepers to deliver biodiversity actions on 24 churches (22 
Catholic Churches and 2 Church of Ireland Churches) in County 
Clare. The initiative has spread through the Heritage Council’s 
Biodiversity Officer network to six other counties including 
Wexford, Leitrim, Louth, Mayo, Cork City and Limerick. The Clare 
biodiversity project featured in national press including RTE News 
and other print media outlets.

Hedgerow and Invasive Species Training Workshop: 
Ennistymon 
Clare County Council’s Biodiversity Officer in conjunction with 
INVAS Biosecurity Ltd. delivered training workshop on the 
sustainable management of hedgerows and best practices in 
the biosecurity and treatment of invasive species to staff in the 
Council Offices in Ennistymon on 16th of June 2026. Staff in 
attendance included General Services Supervisors (SGSS), Senior 
Executive Technicians, Area Engineers and Senior Executive 
Engineers. The training course covered best practices in terms of 
adopting an ‘A-shape’ profile for hedgerows, cutting equipment 
and light trimming of hedgerows. The course covered the 
identification of invasive species, the origin of infestation often 
linked to bridges, movement of soil and garden waste; and the 
soil and stone pathway action plan to promote biosecurity.

First public consultation on Ireland’s draft National 
Nature Restoration Plan 
The National Parks and Wildlife Service (NPWS) has published 
Ireland’s initial draft National Restoration Plan (NRP), which is 
due to be submitted to the European Commission in September 
2026, with a final plan to follow in 2027. Public consultation 
opened on 3rd of June 2026, with responses due by 1st of July 
2026. The plan is a requirement of the EU Nature Restoration 
Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2024/1991), adopted by the 
European Parliament and the Council in 2024. The Regulation is 
the first comprehensive, legally binding framework at EU level 
dedicated specifically to the large-scale restoration of degraded 
ecosystems on land and at sea. Details to make a submission 
on the draft plan can be found at the link: https://www.gov.ie/
en/department-of-housing-local-government-and-heritage/
consultations/first-public-consultation-on-irelands-draft-

Men’s Health Week 2026 in County Clare
Men’s Health Week ran from 15-21 June 2026 with a theme of 
“One Step at a Time”. The purpose of Men’s Health Week 2026 
was to encourage men across County Clare to take proactive 
steps towards improving their physical and mental wellbeing. 
Coordinated by Clare County Council in partnership with the HSE, 
community groups and key stakeholders, the initiative focused on 
raising awareness, fostering open conversations and supporting 
men to access information, services and supports in their local 
communities.
A central feature of the week was a dedicated Clare FM Morning 
Focus discussion series, which led the programme and explored 
key topics including mental wellbeing, stress, nutrition, physical 
activity and community connection.

Clare Older People’s Volunteer Recognition Awards Marked 11 
Years of Celebrating Community Champions.
The Clare Volunteer Recognition Awards were held recently, 
marking the 11th year of the event, and bringing together 
community members, organisations, and supporters to celebrate 
the outstanding dedication and contributions of volunteers. The 
event was organised by the Clare Older People’s Council (OPC) 
and supported by the Clare Age Friendly Programme.
The awards recognised the vital role that volunteers played 
in strengthening communities, supporting older people, and 
enhancing wellbeing across the region. The evening provided an 
opportunity not only to honour individual achievements, but also 
to reflect on the collective impact of volunteerism.
Guests were welcomed and seated by members of the Clare 
Older People’s Council, with the event opened through an 
engaging introduction by master of ceremonies, Mike Hanrahan, 
Clare’s Age Friendly Ambassador, who also presented the work 
of the Music Network’s “Making Music in Clare for over 60’s” 
participants. Musical performances from participants added a 
vibrant and inclusive start to the evening.

The evening was expertly compered by Larry Hally, Chairperson

A key feature of the event was a series of nominee videos, which

Inagh Active Retirement Group
On Friday, 12 June 2026, Clare Age Friendly Programme Manager, 
Shanelle Waring, met with members of the Inagh Active 
Retirement Group to deliver an informative presentation on 
ageing in place, the range of home adaptation grants available, 
and the key objectives of the Clare Age Friendly County Strategy 
2024–2030.
The session outlined how the strategy supports older people to 
live independently within their own homes and communities 
for as long as possible. It also highlighted initiatives aimed at 
enhancing safety, accessibility, and social inclusion, along with 
practical supports to assist individuals in planning for positive 
ageing.
The engagement also provided a valuable forum for discussion, 
where participants shared their experiences and raised 
questions, offering important local perspectives. This interaction 
supports the ongoing commitment of the programme to ensure 
that the voices of older people inform the implementation and 
development of the Age Friendly Strategy across Clare.

sustainable use of natural resources.

CLAR PROJECTS 2024
The following community-focused projects below have recently 
been completed with assistance of funding under the CLAR Grant 
Scheme funded by the Department of Rural and Community 
Development and the Gaeltacht. Each project received funding 
of €50,000. These projects were designed to enhance community 
infrastructure, and improve safety and accessibility
Tulla GAA - Accessibility & Parking Works
Redevelopment works at Dr Daly Park, Tulla, Co. Clare, were 
successfully completed with the assistance of €50,000 in funding 
under the CLÁR 2024 Scheme, significantly enhancing the 
accessibility and safety of this community facility. The project 
delivered key upgrades such as the resurfacing of the terracing 
area, improvements to the main access route to the Pavilion and 
gym, and the creation of accessible car parking spaces adjacent 
to key amenities. The integration of these elements, along with 
the installation of safety barriers and general landscaping works, 
has created a more cohesive and inclusive environment. Building 
on earlier CLÁR 2022 improvements, these works ensure that Dr 
Daly Park continues to meet the needs of a growing community, 
supporting participation in sport and recreation for all.
Kilrush Shamrocks GAA - Upgrades to Walkway
The upgrade works at Kilrush Shamrocks GAA Facility were 
completed with the support of €24,822 under CLAR 2024 and have 
made a real difference to how the grounds are used by both the 
club and the wider community. The project focused on improving 
an existing gravel track that had become uneven and difficult to 
use, turning it into a safe and accessible walking route. Works 
included removing an old, unused scoreboard, preparing and 
levelling the ground, and installing a durable tar and chip surface 
suitable for year-round use. The improved walkway now provides 
a welcoming space for walking and recreation, encouraging 
more people to be active while also creating a shared area that 
supports community wellbeing and social interaction.
Tulla Athletics - Car Parking and bike stands
The improvement works at Tulla Athletic Club were completed 
with the support of €50,000 in funding under the CLÁR 2024 
Scheme, focusing on the development of suitable car parking to 
meet the growing demand for access to this popular community 
facility. The project delivered additional parking spaces, including 
accessible bays for people with disabilities, helping to reduce 
congestion and improve safety for users of the running track 
and walking trail. Bicycle stands were also installed to encourage 
sustainable travel, and native green privet hedging was planted 
to enhance the surrounding environment. Overall, the works 
have improved access, convenience, and inclusivity, making the 
facility more welcoming for the wider community engaging in 
recreation and exercise.
Moy GAA - Community Walkway
The development of the community walking track at Moy GAA 
was completed with the support of €50,000 in funding under the 
CLÁR 2024 Scheme, providing a valuable new amenity for the 
area. The project delivered a 200m accessible tarmac walking 
track adjacent to the local community field, designed to cater for 
people of all ages and abilities. Located close to the existing car 
park for ease of access, the track now offers a safe and welcoming 
space for exercise and recreation. It supports increased physical 
activity, encourages social interaction, and provides an inclusive 
outdoor facility that benefits the wider community, including 
older adults, families, and those with mobility challenges.
Derg Active Alliance - Accessible Lift & Specialised Gym 
Equipment
Works at the Derg Active Alliance Community Centre in Scariff 
were completed with the support of €46,004 in funding under 
the CLÁR Scheme 2024, significantly improving accessibility and 
inclusivity within this important community facility. The project 
focused on ensuring that all users, including those with mobility 
challenges, could fully access and benefit from the centre’s

Crusheen GAA – Car Park Works
 The CLÁR 2024 grant of €50,000 enabled Crusheen GAA Club, 
a key sporting and community hub serving North Clare and 
South Galway, to successfully complete the surfacing of a much-
needed community car park at its grounds. Supporting 25 teams 
across hurling, camogie, and ladies football, as well as a wide 
range of community and recreational initiatives in partnership 
with the nearby Community Centre and National School, the 
Club had been experiencing increasing demand and associated 
parking challenges. Delivered in line with the Club’s long-term 
Masterplan, the project has enhanced the overall functionality 
of the facilities and strengthened their role as a shared, multi-use 
community amenity.

FUND 2024 - PROJECTS
Clare County Council was awarded €2,608,408 under the 
Community Recognition Fund 2024. This fund is specifically 
targeted at projects that are located in towns and villages that 
are hosting the Beneficiaries of Temporary Protection and/or 
International Protection. A total of 29 projects were approved for 
funding under the 2024 Scheme. the following 4 projects funded 
under the scheme have recently been completed.
1.	
Bunratty Search and Rescue Services Ltd received €86,000 
to enhance its emergency response capability through the 
purchase of a new rescue boat and the repair of its existing 
vessel, SRK Saoirse. Established in 1981, the voluntary 
organisation plays a critical role across the Shannon and 
Fergus estuaries, and the upgrade addressed the ageing 
condition of its fleet, significantly improving operational 
reliability and its capacity to respond to emergencies 
and support community water-based events and safety 
education initiatives.
2.	
Kilkee Waterworld was awarded €90,000 to carry out 
essential repair and regrouting works to tiled floor areas 
across public walkways, changing rooms, and the pool deck. 
Following a health and safety assessment that identified 
deterioration posing risks to users, the project delivered 
critical maintenance improvements that enhanced safety 
and extended the lifespan of the facility.
3.	
Ballyvaughan Community Sportsfield was allocated €91,000 
for Phase 2 of its development which involved partially 
enclosing the field with perimeter fencing and resurfacing 
the car park with a tarmac finish. These upgrades improved 
safety, accessibility, and traffic management while creating 
a more structured and user-friendly facility, encouraging 
increased community participation and enhancing the 
overall quality of this important local recreational amenity.
4.	
Liscannor Community Sportsfield received €61,000 to 
improve spectator facilities through the construction of a 
dedicated stand, along with accessible pathways and safety 
lighting. Responding to increased participation in local sports 
and the exposed nature of the site, the project created a 
more comfortable and inclusive environment for spectators, 
encouraging greater community engagement and supporting 
the continued development of sporting activities for all age 
groups.

Planning permission for the extension of Drumcliff Burial Ground 
was granted by An Coimisiún Pleanála on 26 May. The approved 
development comprises approximately 400 additional double 
plots, a columbarium wall with 470 niches, ash plots, car parking, 
footpaths, drainage, and associated site works.

support being provided by the General Design Office. The project 
will progress through the statutory Part 8 planning process in the 
coming months.
UKRAINIAN SERVICES TEAM

 On 26th May, Government announced that the Accommodation

transition for hosts and beneficiaries while the Government 
considers further steps for the scheme’s eventual closure.

Moving Towards a Public Health Approach to Violence 
Intervention
The Chair and staff of the Clare LCSP attended a conference 
on “Moving Towards a Public Health Approach to Violence 
Intervention” on 12th June. Community residents, youth workers, 
service providers, policy makers and people with lived experience 
came together in the Teacher’s Club in Dublin to discuss moving 
towards a public health approach to violence intervention. 
This event marked the first in a planned series aimed at 
strengthening understanding, building capacity and generating 
momentum around community violence intervention. Hosted by 
the Canal Communities Violence Intervention Initiative (CCVII), 
the conference included a detailed discussion on reframing 
perceptions of violence i.e. shifting from a predominantly 
policing-focused response to a more proactive, public health–led 
approach.
One of the key speakers was Karyn McCluskey who was joined on 
stage by Senator Lynn Ruane (Chair of the CCVII Advisory Board) and 
Paul Perth (CCVII Coordinator). 
Karyn, a Scottish forensic psychologist, is the Chief Executive of 
Community Justice Scotland and former Director of the Violence 
Reduction Unit. She is widely recognised for her pioneering work 
with Scotland’s Violence Reduction Unit, which successfully 
reframed violent crime as a preventable public health issue 
rather than solely a matter for law enforcement.
Key themes of the discussion included the practical 
implementation of violence prevention approaches, the need for 
system-wide cultural change and the importance of establishing 
shared responsibility across healthcare services, policymakers 
and local communities.
Particular reference was made to the Canal Communities 
Community-Based Public Safety Strategy which aims to reduce 
violence through targeted, community-focused interventions, 
with a particular emphasis on supporting vulnerable populations. 
The approach centres on relationship-based violence prevention, 
empowering trusted community members and supporting 
community leadership. The strategy identifies key themes, 
including the use of restorative practices to support community 
healing, trauma-informed approaches and strong interagency 
collaboration. It also emphasises making effective use of existing 
community infrastructure to deliver coordinated supports across 
prevention, victim services and recovery. A copy of the full 
strategy is available at
